subject.title: UI/TUI: session-recap block leaks into visible user message rendering

question: Should maintainers replace the conflicting fork PR with a same-repository repair PR, or wait for the fork author to rebase and enable maintainer edits?
rationale: The source-level bug and fix boundary are clear, but the issue is already linked to an open fork PR that is conflicting and not maintainer-modifiable, so automation should not create a duplicate same-problem PR without maintainer routing.

options.title: Replace with upstream fix
options.body: Open or adopt a narrow `openclaw/openclaw` PR, credit the fork work, and close or supersede the fork candidate only after the replacement exists.

options.title: Ask for fork rebase
options.body: Keep waiting on the fork PR and ask the contributor to rebase it onto current main with maintainer-edit settings if possible.

options.title: Leave parked
options.body: Keep the issue paired with the fork PR for now, accepting that the source-reproducible UI/TUI leak remains unresolved.

recommendation.title: Replace with upstream fix
recommendation.body: Open or adopt a narrow `openclaw/openclaw` PR, credit the fork work, and close or supersede the fork candidate only after the replacement exists.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the original shared stripper PR and authored the TUI leading-only stripping path, so they are the best current routing owner for this UI/TUI shared-boundary decision.
